headline: The Financial Stability Board has told G20 finance chiefs that AI is among the risks to the global financial system and has finalised practices for adopting it responsibly.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: an official letter and finalised AI practices from the main international financial-stability body, but the release names no specific AI risk.
importance_line: What changed: the main international coordinator of financial rules has put AI risk before G20 finance ministers and finalised its practices for using AI, which matters first to people whose savings and loans depend on stable banks and markets, then to regulators and banks, but the release does not say what the AI risks are or whether the practices are binding.
summary: The Financial Stability Board (FSB), the international body that coordinates financial regulators from 24 jurisdictions, says in a press release that its chair, Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey, has written to G20 finance ministers and central bank governors naming AI among risks to the global financial system, alongside volatile government bond markets and weak spots in private credit (lending outside the banks). The FSB is also sending the G20 its finalised sound practices for responsible AI adoption and a note on global stablecoins ahead of the ministers' 15 October meeting, and says safe AI adoption will stay on its agenda next year.
notes: Official FSB press release (Ref 12/2026), published 12 Oct 2026.
